newsitem.title: USA: StreamLogic sees Q2 loss at or beyond Q1.
newsitem.headline: StreamLogic sees Q2 loss at or beyond Q1.

text.p: StreamLogic Corp said on Tuesday that revenues for its second quarter ending September 27 will be lower than it expected, and said it will post a loss for the period that will equal or exceed its first-quarter loss.

The company said this month it cut about 10 percent of its U.S. workforce in an effort to control operating expenses. The cost of the job cuts was estimated at $250,000 and will be booked in the second quarter, StreamLogic said.

"However, second-quarter revenues, which include those of the Hammer line of high-performance storage products acquired by the company as of July 1, will be substantially greater than StreamLogic's first-quarter revenues of $11.1 million," the company said in a statement.

"There appears to be a wait-and-see attitude on the part of customers in this industry as new technology offerings begin to be made in the third quarter," J. Larry Smart, StreamLogic president and chief executive, said in the statement.

"This factor, coupled with the typical seasonally slow summer quarter, has negatively impacted revenues this quarter. However, we remain encouraged about the prospects for StreamLogic's current and future products," Smart said.
